skill.name: git-commit
skill.description: Guides an assistant through Git status checks, diff review, staging, conventional commit message creation, and commit verification.
skill.summary: Create conventional Git commits from staged and unstaged changes.
skill.author: 21pounder

content.value_statement: Clear commits take time and require careful diff review. This skill reviews Git changes, creates a conventional message, commits the work, and reports the result.
actual_capabilities: Checks repository state with Git status before committing.
Reviews staged and unstaged diffs to understand the change set.
Infers a Conventional Commits type and optional scope from the changes.
Stages relevant files when needed for the requested commit.
Creates the commit and reports the message and commit hash.
Guides the assistant to avoid committing credentials or .env files.
limitations: Requires a Git repository and permission to run local Git commands.
Does not perform a full code review or test suite analysis.
May need user confirmation when unrelated changes are present.
Cannot guarantee that already staged sensitive files are safe.

use_cases.title: Commit Feature Work
use_cases.description: Create a concise conventional commit after finishing a feature branch.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository History
use_cases.description: Keep commit messages consistent across a project that uses Conventional Commits.

use_cases.title: Review Before Saving Work
use_cases.description: Inspect staged and unstaged changes before creating a local commit.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Current Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit my current changes with a clear conventional commit message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when all current changes should be committed together.

prompt_templates.title: Use A Commit Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a fix commit for the current changes after checking the diff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you know the desired Conventional Commits type.

prompt_templates.title: Add Scope And Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit these changes with scope auth and a concise message based on the diff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a project area should appear in the commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Review And Select Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Review staged and unstaged changes, stage only relevant files, then create a conventional commit with a concise explanation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the working tree may contain unrelated edits.

output_examples.output: Created a conventional commit for the current change set. Reported the commit message and new commit hash.

output_examples.input: Create a fix commit for the authentication update.
output_examples.output: Reviewed the diff, used a fix type with auth scope, committed the update, and reported success.

output_examples.input: Stage relevant files and commit the docs update.
output_examples.output: Selected the documentation files, created a docs commit, and confirmed the working tree status.

best_practices: Review the reported files before approving a commit.
Use explicit type and scope when the change category is known.
Run tests before committing behavior changes.
anti_patterns: Do not commit unrelated changes in one commit.
Do not include credentials, .env files, or private keys.
Do not use amend or force workflows unless explicitly requested.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the assistant to inspect changes, prepare a message, run the commit, and report the result.

faq.question: Does it support Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for messages that follow type, optional scope, and concise description.

faq.question: Can I provide my own commit message?
faq.answer: Yes. The parameters include an optional message override for user supplied commit text.

faq.question: Will it avoid sensitive files?
faq.answer: The guidance tells the assistant not to commit .env files, credentials, or similar secrets.

faq.question: Does it push commits to a remote?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow creates a local commit and reports the result.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
